verdict.rationale: Babylon.js documents sprites and layers as part of its scene graph, so it has some native 2D building blocks. Everything else in the evidence points to a 3D-first engine: its physics integrations (Havok, Cannon.js, Ammo.js, Oimo.js) are 3D engines, and the 2D GUI system is a UI layer, not a 2D game workflow. Missing for 10: tilemap support, 2D physics, evidence that 2D is a first-class workflow rather than an add-on to 3D, and depth on sprite tooling or independent corroboration.
